draft.title: First Nations wellbeing and Closing the Gap
card: Gaps remain between First Nations people and other Australians in health, education and jobs. Examples include life expectancy, school completion and employment.
These gaps are linked to past and present unequal treatment, including the effects of dispossession. They are not caused by First Nations cultures.
Closing the Gap is an agreement between Australian governments and First Nations organisations. It sets shared targets to improve outcomes in areas such as health, education and jobs.
First Nations communities are partners in the agreement, not only recipients of programs. Their knowledge and leadership help shape what is done.
draft.remember: Closing the Gap sets shared targets, with First Nations communities as partners.

opts: An agreement with shared targets set with First Nations partners
A program run by governments without First Nations input
A law that makes outcomes equal in every community
A report that only measures wellbeing in cities
a.why: Closing the Gap sets shared targets, and First Nations communities and organisations are partners in it. It is not run by governments alone. It is also an agreement with targets, not a law that makes outcomes equal.
a.clue: Think about who is involved in making the agreement.

b.q: A council wants to improve jobs for First Nations people in its region. Which approach best matches the Closing the Gap partnership idea?
opts: Plan the program together with local First Nations leaders
Design the program first, then tell the community about it
Copy a program from a city without asking anyone
Leave the program to outside experts to decide alone
b.why: The partnership idea means First Nations communities help shape what is done. Planning with local leaders does this. Telling the community afterwards treats it as a recipient, which is the approach the agreement moves away from.
b.clue: Who should help shape the plan from the start?

card: Gaps remain between First Nations people and other Australians in health, education and jobs. Examples include life expectancy, school completion and employment.
These gaps are linked to past and present unequal treatment, including the effects of dispossession. They are not caused by First Nations cultures.
Closing the Gap is an agreement between Australian governments and First Nations organisations. It sets shared targets to improve outcomes in areas such as health, education and jobs.

proposal.remember: Closing the Gap sets shared targets, with First Nations communities as partners.

a.q: Which best describes Closing the Gap?
opts: Targets agreed by governments and First Nations groups
Targets set by governments alone for First Nations groups
A law that requires equal outcomes in every community
A survey ranking wellbeing in First Nations communities
a.why: Closing the Gap is an agreement, and its targets are shared between governments and First Nations organisations. Targets set by governments alone would treat communities as recipients, not partners. It is also not a law or a survey.
a.clue: Think about who sets the targets.

b.q: A council wants to improve jobs for First Nations people in its region. Which approach best matches the Closing the Gap partnership idea?
opts: Plan it with local First Nations leaders from the start
Design it, then ask First Nations leaders for feedback
Have experts design a job program for First Nations people
Copy a First Nations job program that worked in a city
b.why: The partnership idea means First Nations communities help shape what is done from the start. Asking for feedback after the program is designed is tempting, but the plan is already made, so the community is treated more as a recipient than a partner.
b.clue: When do local leaders get a say in the plan?
